question.prompt:
For how many paths consisting of a sequence of horizontal and/or vertical line segments, with each segment connecting a pair of adjacent letters in the diagram below, is the word CONTEST spelled out as the path is traversed from beginning to end?

[Figure 1](figures/1977_AMC_12_Q20_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Read the letters backward, starting from the final \(T\). This makes the direction choices especially simple. The only \(T\) adjacent to an \(S\) is the bottom central \(T\), so every complete path must end there.

Starting there and spelling \(T,S,E,T,N,O,C\), each move must be upward or horizontally away from the center. A downward move or a horizontal move toward the center gives the wrong next letter. Once a path moves horizontally, it stays on that side of the diagram.

First count reversed paths in the left half, including the central column. At each of the six steps, choose either up or left. Every sequence of six choices is valid: after \(u\) upward moves and \(h\) leftward moves, the current row is \(6-u\) rows below the top and the position is \(h\) columns left of center. It remains inside the triangular diagram because \(h\leq6-u\) whenever \(u+h\leq6\). Each move supplies the next required letter, and after six moves the path reaches a boundary \(C\).

Thus there are \(2^6=64\) paths in the left half, and likewise 64 in the right half. A choice sequence determines exactly one path, so neither half-count repeats a path. The only path belonging to both halves is the entirely vertical one. All paths lie in at least one half, so the total is
\[
64+64-1=\boxed{127}.
\]
This is none of choices A through D, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Reverse the paths and count the two halves

solutions.explanation:
Count paths forward by writing at each letter the number of ways to reach it while spelling the required beginning of CONTEST. Give every boundary \(C\) the count 1. At each later letter, add the counts at all adjacent letters that can precede it. This includes every path exactly once, because its final step identifies a unique preceding position.

To organize these additions, number the letter stages \(0,1,\ldots,6\), corresponding to \(C,O,N,T,E,S,T\). Each stage has one letter in the central column and, except at the final stage, letters on the two sloping arms below it.

At stage 0, every count is 1. For an off-center letter at any later stage, the two possible preceding letters are the one directly above it and the one immediately farther from the center. Both are off-center letters of the previous stage. Thus the off-center counts double at each stage: they are \(1,2,4,8,16,32\) for \(C,O,N,T,E,S\), respectively.

Let \(t_j\) be the count at the central letter of stage \(j\). Its possible predecessors are the central letter above it and the two letters immediately beside it. Those side letters each have count \(2^{j-1}\). Hence
\[
t_0=1,\qquad t_j=t_{j-1}+2\cdot2^{j-1}
=t_{j-1}+2^j.
\]
Successive central counts are therefore
\[
1,\ 3,\ 7,\ 15,\ 31,\ 63,\ 127.
\]
The only possible final \(T\) is the bottom central one, since the other \(T\)'s are not adjacent to an \(S\). Its count is \(\boxed{127}\), giving choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Add the counts arriving at each letter
Count each half and subtract the overlap
